payload.reason: The evidence provides specific references to previous works that are compared to the current research, detailing their approaches to integrating morphological information in translation models.

claims.text: Previous work considered morphological information for both SMT and NMT, including methods for integrating word-level annotation and addressing data sparsity.
BIBREF8 proposed an effective way to integrate word-level annotation in SMT, which can be morphological, syntactic, or semantic.
BIBREF9 decomposed the process of translating a word into two steps, producing a stem and selecting an appropriate inflection using a discriminative model.
BIBREF10 used distributed representations for words and soft morphological tags in their neural inflection model to reduce lexical sparsity.
